meal.title: Program vs. Process
meal.objective: Distinguish a static program from a running process

voice.script: What happens when you double‑click an app? When you open a file, the operating system loads its instructions into memory. Those instructions are called a program – a static set of code that sits on disk. The moment the OS starts executing that code, it becomes a process. A process is the program while it is alive, with its own memory, registers, and a place on the CPU schedule. In other words, a program is the recipe, a process is the chef actually cooking. This distinction matters because the scheduler only sees processes, not raw files. Now let's look at a tiny script. When you run it, you will see the name appear on the screen. Remember: a program is code, a process is that code in action. Try writing a short text file and then run it with Python to see the difference.
